advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Avoid emitting SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE twice in the bounded-retry prompt (schema_hint already ends with it via schema_directive).
evidence: structured.py:105-112 schema_directive returns schema text `+ "\n\n" + SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE`
advisory.finding: The bounded-retry prompt now contains SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE twice: `schema_hint` is `structured.schema_directive(model_cls)`, which after this change already ends with `\n\n` + SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE, yet the retry prompt interpolates `{schema_hint}` and then also appends `{structured.SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE}` a second time. The marker instruction is duplicated in the same prompt turn.
scenarios: Any bounded retry (layer 4) after a first-attempt parse failure sends the sentinel directive twice to the model.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the trailing `{structured.SENTINEL_DIRECTIVE}` from the retry prompt (schema_hint already carries it), or reword the retry tail to reference the markers without re-appending the full directive.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the retry-prompt 'no bare JSON' assertion effective (it is currently a tautology because _OPEN is always present).
evidence: test_structured_run.py: `assert _OPEN in retry_prompt and _END in retry_prompt` (earlier in same test)

test_structured_run.py: `assert "no code fence" not in retry_prompt or _OPEN in retry_prompt` — since _OPEN is guaranteed present, the `or _OPEN in retry_prompt` clause makes the whole assertion unconditionally true
`assert "no code fence" not in retry_prompt or _OPEN in retry_prompt`

Line 210 already asserts: `assert _OPEN in retry_prompt and _END in retry_prompt` — so `_OPEN in retry_prompt` is guaranteed True by the time line 214 runs, making the `or _OPEN in retry_prompt` disjunct unconditionally true.
Regression-blindness: if the retry tail regressed to re-append the old 'no code fence' bare-JSON wording ALONGSIDE the markers, this assertion would still pass, so it cannot detect that regression.
advisory.finding: The final assertion in the new retry test is a tautology and provides no coverage: `assert "no code fence" not in retry_prompt or _OPEN in retry_prompt`. `_OPEN` is always present in the retry prompt (the test already asserts this two lines above), so the right-hand disjunct is always True and the assertion can never fail regardless of whether a bare-JSON 'no code fence' instruction is present.
merged_from: The final assertion in test_bounded_retry_prompt_names_the_markers_not_bare_json is vacuous: `assert "no code fence" not in retry_prompt or _OPEN in retry_prompt` can never fail because line 210 already asserted `_OPEN in retry_prompt` is True, making the right-hand disjunct always satisfied. It provides no regression coverage for its stated intent (that the retry prompt no longer tells the model to emit bare JSON with 'no code fence').
scenarios: A regression that reintroduces a bare-JSON 'no code fence' instruction alongside the markers would not be caught by this assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert on the absence of the old markerless wording directly, e.g. `assert "no code fence" not in retry_prompt` (the current directive uses 'no markdown fence'), so a reverted retry tail turns the test red.
